questions.stem: Which city replaced Yangon as the official capital of Myanmar in 2005–06 when the military junta relocated the seat of government?

options.option_text: Naypyidaw, the purpose-built planned capital city
Mandalay, the second-largest city in Myanmar
Bago, formerly known as Pegu in colonial records
Mawlamyine, a major port city in Mon State

questions.explanation: Naypyidaw was declared Myanmar's capital in November 2005 when the military government moved administrative functions from Yangon. Mandalay is the most tempting wrong answer because it served as the last royal capital before British annexation in 1885, but it was never chosen as the modern administrative capital.

questions.stem: The currency 'Ringgit' is the official monetary unit of which Southeast Asian country?

options.option_text: Indonesia, where the national currency is the Rupiah
Malaysia, a federal constitutional monarchy in SE Asia
Thailand, where the national currency is called the Baht
Philippines, where the national currency is the Peso

questions.explanation: The Ringgit (MYR) is Malaysia's official currency. Indonesia, Malaysia's neighbour and the region's most populous country, uses the Rupiah — the most common wrong answer as students frequently mix up Southeast Asian currencies.

questions.stem: The unicameral parliament of which Nordic country is called the 'Folketing' and meets in Christiansborg Palace?

options.option_text: Sweden, whose parliament is officially called the Riksdag
Finland, whose parliament is officially called the Eduskunta
Denmark, the Scandinavian kingdom bordering Germany
Iceland, whose parliament is the ancient Althing

questions.explanation: Denmark's unicameral legislature is the Folketing, seated at Christiansborg Palace in Copenhagen. Sweden's parliament, the Riksdag, is the most common wrong answer because both are Scandinavian and the names sound phonetically similar; Finland's Eduskunta and Iceland's Althing are also plausible Nordic distractors.

questions.stem: The currency 'Kwanza' is the official monetary unit of which major oil-producing African nation?

options.option_text: Angola, a major oil-producing nation in southern Africa
Mozambique, located on the southeastern African coast
Zambia, which uses a phonetically similar currency called Kwacha
Kenya, where the official currency is the East African Shilling

questions.explanation: The Kwanza (AOA) is Angola's official currency. Zambia's Kwacha (ZMW) is the most dangerous distractor because the names are phonetically very close; candidates must not confuse the two. Mozambique uses the Metical and Kenya uses the Shilling.

questions.stem: Which of the following European Union member states does NOT use the Euro as its official currency?

options.option_text: Croatia, which joined the Eurozone on 1 January 2023
Slovakia, which adopted the Euro in 2009 after EU entry
Slovenia, among the first post-Yugoslav states to use Euro
Sweden, which still retains its own Krona after a 2003 referendum

questions.explanation: Sweden is an EU member since 1995 but rejected Euro adoption in a 2003 referendum and continues to use the Swedish Krona (SEK). Croatia is the trickiest distractor — it is the newest Eurozone member (joined January 2023), so students often doubt it, but it has legally adopted the Euro.

questions.stem: The 'Althing' (Alþingi), widely regarded as the world's oldest continuously operating parliament established in 930 AD, belongs to which country?

options.option_text: Greenland, a self-governing Danish autonomous territory
Iceland, a Nordic island nation settled by Norse Vikings
Faroe Islands, a North Atlantic archipelago under Denmark
Norway, whose Storting has functioned continuously since 1814

questions.explanation: Iceland's Althing, founded in 930 AD at Þingvellir by Norse settlers, is recognised as the world's oldest parliament still in operation. Norway's Storting (1814) is the most tempting wrong answer because it is old and well-known, but it is nearly 900 years younger than the Althing. Greenland and the Faroe Islands have their own legislatures but are not sovereign states.

questions.stem: Which country's parliament is officially called the 'Grand National Assembly' (Büyük Millet Meclisi), founded by Mustafa Kemal Atatürk in 1920 in Ankara?

options.option_text: Greece, whose unicameral parliament is called the Vouli
Hungary, whose parliament is the Országgyűlés in Budapest
Türkiye (Turkey), straddling the European and Asian continents
Romania, which has a bicameral legislature seated in Bucharest

questions.explanation: Türkiye's parliament, the Grand National Assembly (Türkiye Büyük Millet Meclisi), was founded on 23 April 1920 in Ankara by Atatürk during the Turkish War of Independence. Hungary's National Assembly (Országgyűlés) is the most dangerous distractor because students confuse 'National Assembly' with 'Grand National Assembly'; however, Hungary's legislature is never called 'Grand' — that distinctive title belongs to Türkiye.
